title: Brits nearly twice as likely to spot pressure tactics in horror films as investment red flags
summary: Investors are almost twice as likely to recognise pressure tactics in a horror film as they are when those tactics are used to promote an investment opportunity, new FCA data suggests. A survey of UK 18 to 40-year-olds who own or are considering investments found 65% spotted ‘this is your only chance’ as a classic horror warning sign. But when faced with a ‘last chance to buy’ investment opportunity, only 36% said it would make them more cautious, while 37% said they would feel pressure to buy quickly or risk missing out. The pattern also holds for other pressure tactics. While 59% recognised countdowns like the ticking clock in 'Saw' as a tactic designed to make characters act rashly, just 5% said they would be suspicious of the pressure created by a rising investment price graph.Blind spots show up with novelty, too. Nearly half (47%) recognised that horror sequels often bring back familiar threats disguised as something new. Yet only 12% were similarly sceptical of a 'groundbreaking new' investment product, while 1 in 10 said being new would actually make them more likely to invest. title: Foreign exchange transactions in November 2026
summary: Norges Bank carries out foreign exchange transactions on behalf of the government and to fund the transfer of dividends and interest payments to the government. In November 2026, the daily net purchases of foreign exchange for these purposes will amount to NOK 176 million. The net amount arises from Norges Bank needing to purchase foreign currency equivalent to 300 million NOK per day on behalf of the government while simultaneously needing to sell foreign currency equivalent to 124 million NOK per day to fund the transfer of dividends and interest payments to the government.

title: Neue Studie untersucht jüngsten Anstieg der Inflationsrate
summary: Eine neue Studie der Bundesbank untersucht den aktuellen Verlauf der deutschen Inflationsrate im Vergleich zur Hochinflationsphase um das Jahr 2022. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass der aktuelle Schock sich anders zusammensetzt als 2022, eine Wiederholung der Hochinflationsphase erscheint daher unwahrscheinlich. Trotzdem dürfte die Inflationsrate in Deutschland bis ins nächste Jahr hinein merklich erhöht bleiben.

title: Global Review concludes with a declaration on partnerships for trade and development
summary: Marking the 20th anniversary of the Aid for Trade Initiative, WTO members adopted a declaration on 30 October repositioning the initiative as "Aid for Trade: partnerships for trade and development". The declaration was adopted at a meeting of the Committee on Trade and Development, which wrapped up the two-day 10th Global Review of Aid for Trade held at WTO headquarters in Geneva.

title: New report looks at role of South-South and triangular cooperation for trade development
summary: The growing importance of trade between developing economies - South-South trade - is highlighted in a joint publication launched on Day 1 (29 October) of the 10th Global Review of Aid for Trade by the WTO and the United Nations Office for South-South Cooperation (UNOSSC). The publication examines how the partnerships fostered through South-South cooperation and triangular cooperation – South-South partnerships supported by a developed economy - are helping strengthen developing economies' trade capacities and facilitate market access.

title: WHO, WIPO and the WTO to hold 13th Joint Technical Symposium on 25 November 2026
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO), the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) and the World Trade Organization (WTO) will hold the 13th Joint Technical Symposium on Enabling Ecosystems for Local and Regional Health Products Manufacturing: Considering the Role of Trade, IP, AI and Digital Innovation on 25 November 2026, hosted by WHO at the International Conference Centre Geneva (CICG). The deadline for registration is 23 November 2026.

title: Members review regional trade agreements, confirm meeting frequency, adopt annual report
summary: At a meeting of the Committee on Regional Trade Agreements (CRTA) on 29 October, WTO members considered five regional trade agreements (RTAs) among members as well as three involving non-members. They also took note of new RTA notifications and adopted the Committee's annual report for 2026.
